•AUTHOR: Mil HART

Oh I do love these types of books. The 
objective in brief is to prove that 
mankind is a seeded race put here by 
extraterrestrials and that essentially the 
stories in the Bible are true except that 
you replace the word "God" with "ET". 
Far fetched? Ridiculous? Burn the heretic 
at the stake? Well Will Hat isn't the first to 
put forward such theories in recent times 
and he won't be the last, Who's going to 
be offended the most? Well, Creationists 
will rejoice in that he picks insightful holes 
in Darwin's Theory Of Evolution but the let 
down for them is that he inevitably 
arrives at a different conclusion, 
Darwinists, already slowly on the retreat, 
will shrug their shoulders end take yet 
another step backwards into the shad-
ows that they have begun habituating. 
I'll give them another twenty yeas or 
maybe less before we begin to look 
upon them in the same way we look 
upon The Flat Earth Sociely. 
Yes, things really are 
changing that fast, 
because of 
you've 
guessed it, science! 
Darwin himself knew of 
the Achilles heel in his 
theory, which is that there 
is no fossil evidence of 
intermediate links h the 
evolution of Evolution. 
In other words, there is no 
record of those species 
that would have devel-
oped under Darwin's the-
ory but failed owing to 
the "survival of the fittest" 
dictum. 
And there should be 
loads of evidence. 
Hence the term "The 
Missing Link." It's actually 
missing links. 
In fact these doubts about Darwin have 
even been breaking out into the main-
stream media and more than once I 
have read that random mutation and 
natural selection cannot account for the 
complexities of Life. It is true that Darwin 
never actually addressed the origin of 
Life itself, preferring rather to pick things 
up after that point. Nevertheless, you 
might already be wary of reading 
astronomer Fred Hoyle's now infamous 
statement about the chances of Life 
originating in an organic soup being as 
likely as the assembly of a fully function-
ing 747 by a whirlwind passing through 
a junkyard. So, thanks for the last 150 
years Charlie but we now need to be 
considering other possibilities about how 
we got here. Shame really. It was a nice 
comfortable idea that seemed to fit but 
the holes the author blows in it are just 
too big to patch up. 
Okay. So perhaps we didn't crawl out of 
the "soup" to start off with and maybe 
we didn't move along after that as 
Darwin proposed. So what other alterna-
tives are there? At the moment, to be 
precise, two. The more scientifically 
inclined theory is Panspermia as originat-
ed by the Swedish physicist Svante 
Arrhenius in the nineteenth century and 
developed further by Francis Crick the 
co-discoverer of the structure of DNA. 
Crick proposed that Life was seeded on 
Earth by spores from outer space that 
got here via rockets from another planet 
where Life had evolved to a higher 
technical level beyond where even we 
are today. I do not know how Life was 
meant to have formed originally on this 
other planet first but that, for the 
moment, is by the by 
Lata, Fred Hoyle and his colleague N. 
Chandra Wickramasinghe claimed that 
these spores got here on the back of 
comets that crashed to earth, a theory 
that was greeted with ridicule, in fact 
Wickramasinghe recently claimed that 
the SARS virus might have got to earth in 
a similar way too. 
What gradually gave these theories 
some credence and scientific accept-
ability was the result of an accidental 
experiment. The bacterium Streptococcus 
Mitus, a throat 
infection, inad-
vertently hitch-
ed a ride to the 
moon in the 
late 60s on 
board one of 
the cameras 
mounted on 
the Surveyor 3 
landing mod-
ule. The Apollo 
12 mission res-

cued it safely 
without leaving

any contami-
nation behind 
® * 
and when 
brought back 
to Earth it was 
discovered that 
the bacteria 
had survived 
and was still 
viable. And that 
was after more than a year of sitting on 
the moon in a very inhospitable environ-
ment. This added a lot of credence to 
the Panspermia argument. Life it 
seemed could survive the extreme cold 
and intense levels of radiation in outer 
space. 
Hart spends a bit of time on these theo-
ries and obviously has some respect for 
them. But they are not his way. He is 
struck by the sudden and dramatic 
increase in human innovation and activ-
ity from around 3,500 BC in six key areas 
around the world: Mexico, Peru, Egypt, 
Sumer, the Indus Valley and China. 
The 
GENESIS 
RACE 
Our Extraterrestrial DNA 
arid the True Origins of the Species 
Here could be seen the construction of 
monumental structures, the formation of 
towns, the move to agriculture away 
from hunter gathering, organised work-
forces, specialist skills, and, especially in 
Sumer, an intellectual development that 
was triiy breadth taking. In Sumer (mod-
ern day Iraq) they invented irrigation, 
kilns, writing, the wheel, bronze, the char-
iot, sailboats, mathematics, astrology, 
schools, and the concept of a trade or 
profession. Pretly well the entire founda-
tion of future human civilisation. Bearing 
in mind that humans only 500 hundred 
miles away were still living in mud huts 
and had no idea about sticking a seed 
in the ground and watching it gow, you 
have to ask, why the vast disparity? 
These places stood outfrom the rest of 
the world in very sharp contrast. What 
was going on there to cause all this? 
The creation myths from these geo-
graphically unconnected areas are very 
similar. Gods, appearing as superior 
humans, descended from the heavens 
and created human beings as we now 
are, and gave them civilisation. Hart 
believes all this was caused by "intelli-
gent extraterrestrial intervention". Not one 
of these lost civilisations claims in their 
creation myths that they themselves dis-
covered the talents that made them so 
unique. They all claimed it came from 
the Gods. 
After Sumer, he takes a look at Egypt 
and in particular focuses on the Great 
Pyramid and The Sphinx and specifically, 
the uncertainty about how these pro-
jects were built He implies strongly that 
we would have difficulty building a pro-
ject like that even today and while vari-
ous archaeologists have offered expla-
nations and even tried practical experi-
ments to demonstrate how they were 
built, he remains unconvinced So who 
built them? 
There is also the little matter of the Great 
Pyramid's properties. It is a geodesic 
marker of the centre of the earth's land-
mass (facing due north) and the ratio of 
its height to its perimeter equals the ratio 
of the earth's radius to its circumference. 
Pi is incorporated in various features. 
Little is known about the Water People of 
the Indus Valley, heated in southeastern 
Pakistan and western India. This is mainly 
due to the fact that we haven't been 
able, yet, to decipher their language 
and many of their discovered cities have 
yet to be excavated. They appeared at 
around 3000 BC and like the Sumerians, 
they built two story buildings in brick and 
stone, developed sewer systems, streets, 
and even put up the first ever billboard. 
Unfortunately, we can't read it! They 
seemed to dsplay a similar level of 
development to Sumer and there is evi-
dence of the two groups trading, They 
were peaceful and multi racial and 
seemed able to spread themselves and 
expand over a considerable area with-
out violence, They also appeared very 
egalitarian, as there is no evidence of 
gand palaces and large, exclusive homes. 
There is for me in this chapter an inter-
esting reference that allows me to look 
a little more objectively at what Hart 
Reviewed by Stuart Miller 
writes here. He makes mention of India's 
National Institute of Oceanography and 
their discovery in 2000 of some anom-
alous objects 80 feet under water off 
the Coromandel Coast. They called in 
Graham Hancock to take a closer look 
and Graham made a fascinating docu-
mentary on the project that I remember 
well from a couple of years ago. They 
were looking for iost cities and based on 
what Graham filmed and showed us, I 
had no doubt that that was exactly 
what he had found, and not just there 
either. But the programme was balanced 
and offered other points of view, and 
experts were called in who disagreed 
with Graham's interpretation. Hart makes 
no mention of this and takes the evi-
dence of Graham's discoveries and 
assessment as a given fact, 
The chapter on China is, quite simply, 
fascinating. It is not well known that there 
are about 100 pyramids located in a 70 
mile radus of the city of Xian. Only one 
westerner, a German by the name of 
Hausdorf, has been able to briefly see 
them back in 1994. As is tiresomely 
usual, the Chinese government remains 
extremely wary of letting anyone near 
them and apparently has not attempted 
to investigate them themselves, Hausdorf 
is convinced they're hiding something. 
But the really fascinating part of this 
chapter is a story that Hart acknowl-
edges is extremely difficult to verify. 
It's not the first time I've come across this 
tale but there is more detail here than 
I've read before. It involves the 1938 dis-
covery of a number of strange skeletons 
near the Chinese border with Tibet.

cannot tell if the contents are true, partially

ber of insiders who had waked on UFO

brought into the public domain people 
like Salter who would otherwise have
